issues.legal_issue: Estrangement and statements of disinterest do not establish that a member has separated from a Hindu joint family without an unequivocal and communicated intention to separate.
material_facts: A father and his sons were members of a Hindu joint family, although the family itself owned no property and the properties at issue were the father’s self-acquired property.
The father and one son had a history of serious disagreement, and the son sometimes said that he was not interested in his father’s estate.
The evidence did not establish that the son made an unequivocal declaration of separation or communicated an intention to separate to the family.
The other son, who alleged separation, relied on vague evidence that did not establish it.
issues.conclusion: The son had not separated from the family and was not excluded from sharing in the estate on that ground.
issues.legal_principle: The law presumes members of a Hindu family to be joint, with a stronger presumption between a father and his sons. The party alleging separation bears the burden of proving it satisfactorily. A Hindu joint family need not own property; relationship, rather than property, binds its members. Separation requires more than emotional statements or estrangement; the evidence must establish an unequivocal intention to separate communicated to the family. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this ruling.

rule.if: partition_proceeding and hindu_joint_family_relationship and separation_claim and separation_declaration_absent

predicates.partition_proceeding: A person sought a division of property on the basis of membership in a family.
predicates.hindu_joint_family_relationship: The disputing family members were related as members of a Hindu family, including as a father and son.
predicates.separation_claim: A family member alleged that another member had separated from the family.
predicates.separation_declaration_absent: The evidence did not show an unequivocal declaration of separation communicated to the family.

issues.definition: When a separation claim arises in a partition proceeding involving a Hindu joint family, the absence of an unequivocal communicated separation declaration means separation is not proved.

issues.legal_issue: Transferring a depositor’s fixed deposits into joint names does not establish a gift or advancement to the other named person without proof of an intention to benefit that person exclusively.
material_facts: The father held fixed deposits in his own name and was alleged to have instructed the bank and a company to place deposits in his and one son’s joint names shortly before his death.
The evidence did not satisfactorily establish that the alleged instructions were genuine.

Even assuming the instructions were given, they referred to the father’s serious illness and did not establish an intention to benefit the son exclusively; the transfers could have been intended to facilitate collection.
The father remained the owner of the deposits until his death, and there was no proven general intention to benefit the son through the transfers.
issues.conclusion: The alleged transfers did not establish a gift or advancement to the son, and the deposits remained part of the father’s estate.
issues.legal_principle: There is no presumption of advancement in India. A person claiming an advancement must prove both a genuine transfer and a general intention to benefit the recipient, together with a transfer made in pursuance of that intention. In the absence of proof of a contrary intention, a deposit in joint names does not by itself give the other named person beneficial ownership; the depositor retains the beneficial interest. The Court relied on Guran Ditta v. Ram Ditta, Pandit Shambhu Nath Shivpuri v. Pandit Pushkar Nath, Young v. Sealey, Mrs. Avis Fitzalah Cowdrey v. Imperial Bank of India, and Dalvi Nagarajamma v. State Bank of India.

rule.if: partition_proceeding and fixed_deposits_transferred_to_joint_names and depositor_retained_ownership_until_death and exclusive_benefit_intention_not_proved

predicates.partition_proceeding: A person sought a division of an estate in a partition proceeding.
predicates.fixed_deposits_transferred_to_joint_name: A depositor’s fixed deposits were allegedly placed in the depositor’s name jointly with another person.
predicates.depositor_retained_ownership_until_death: The depositor continued to own and control the deposits until death.
predicates.exclusive_benefit_intention_not_proved: The evidence did not establish that the depositor intended the other named person to receive the deposits exclusively.

issues.definition: In a partition proceeding, a joint-name transfer of fixed deposits while the depositor retains ownership until death does not establish a gift or advancement if an intention to benefit the other named person exclusively is not proved.

issues.legal_issue: A genuine cheque issued by a conscious donor to a recipient may constitute a gift when the circumstances establish that the donor intended to give the money.
material_facts: The father issued a genuine cheque for money recovered from a debtor in favour of one son.
Reliable evidence established that the father was conscious when he issued the cheque.
The circumstances, including the son’s assistance to the father, supported the finding that the father intended to give the money to him.
issues.conclusion: The money transferred by cheque was a gift to the son and was his exclusive property.
issues.legal_principle: The Court inferred donative intent from the genuine cheque, the donor’s consciousness when issuing it, and the surrounding circumstances. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this ruling.

rule.if: partition_proceeding and donor_conscious_when_issuing_cheque and genuine_cheque_issued_to_recipient and recipient_helped_donor

predicates.partition_proceeding: A person sought a division of an estate in a partition proceeding.
predicates.donor_conscious_when_issuing_cheque: The person transferring the money was conscious when issuing the cheque.
predicates.genuine_cheque_issued_to_recipient: The transferor issued a genuine cheque in favour of the recipient.
predicates.recipient_helped_donor: The recipient had been helpful to the transferor.

issues.definition: In a partition proceeding, a genuine cheque issued by a conscious donor to a recipient who had helped the donor constitutes a gift when those circumstances support an intention to give.

issues.legal_issue: A deposit made in a recipient’s name, communicated to the recipient, and followed by delivery of the deposit receipt may establish a gift when the evidence supports the donor’s intention to benefit the recipient.
material_facts: The father-in-law deposited money in his daughter-in-law’s name.
He informed her that he had made the deposit and later gave her the deposit receipt.
The evidence that he was fond of her and intended to give her the money was accepted.
issues.conclusion: The deposit was a gift to the daughter-in-law and her exclusive property.
issues.legal_principle: The Court accepted the evidence of the deposit in the recipient’s name, the donor’s communication of it, and his later delivery of the receipt as establishing an intended gift. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this ruling.

rule.if: partition_proceeding and deposit_made_in_recipient_name and donor_informed_recipient_of_deposit and donor_delivered_deposit_receipt and evidence_supports_intention_to_benefit_recipient

predicates.partition_proceeding: A person sought a division of an estate in a partition proceeding.
predicates.deposit_made_in_recipient_name: The depositor placed the money in the recipient’s name.
predicates.donor_informed_recipient_of_deposit: The depositor told the recipient that the deposit had been made.
predicates.donor_delivered_deposit_receipt: The depositor later handed the recipient the receipt for the deposit.
predicates.evidence_supports_intention_to_benefit_r: The evidence supported an intention by the depositor to benefit the recipient.

issues.definition: In a partition proceeding, a deposit made in the recipient’s name, disclosed to the recipient, and followed by delivery of its receipt is a gift when the evidence supports an intention to benefit the recipient.

issues.legal_issue: A court may direct a receiver holding estate property to make a provisional distribution to a claimant who has been kept out of the estate, subject to adjustment in the final decree.
material_facts: One son had been kept out of the father’s estate for many years.
The other son held the properties as receiver.
The excluded son sought a share of the cash in the estate, and the Court considered a provisional payment or transfer of deposits reasonable, with adjustment at the final decree.
issues.conclusion: The receiver was directed to pay the claimant a provisional sum or transfer deposits of equivalent value, subject to adjustment when the final decree was made.
issues.legal_principle: The Court granted a provisional distribution in the circumstances of the partition proceeding and made it subject to adjustment in the final decree. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this direction.

rule.if: partition_proceeding and estate_property_held_by_receiver and claimant_kept_out_of_estate and provisional_distribution_found_reasonable

predicates.partition_proceeding: A person sought a division of an estate in a partition proceeding.
predicates.estate_property_held_by_receiver: A receiver held property belonging to the estate.
predicates.claimant_kept_out_of_estate: A person claiming a share had been kept out of the estate.
predicates.provisional_distribution_found_reasonabl: The court found a provisional distribution to the claimant reasonable, subject to later adjustment.

issues.definition: In a partition proceeding, a receiver holding estate property must make a provisional distribution when the claimant has been kept out of the estate and the court finds that distribution reasonable, subject to adjustment in the final decree.
